$comment: What thematiq does with every entry of nextcloud-variables.json. Edited by hand; the extractor never touches it.
status: mapped (thematiq sets it, via its own stylesheets or because Nextcloud derives it from a value thematiq writes),
settable (a token exists and a set or the admin may give it a value), or excluded (with a reason).
classDefaults gives the status of every icon, runtime and unread entry: the class rule itself is the decision there.
Every theme, component, slot and conduction entry needs its own line, so a property a new Nextcloud release adds
fails npm run test:inventory until someone decides what to do with it.
foreign: names thematiq sets that Nextcloud does not know, each with the reason it is set anyway.
baseline: the names per class that are mapped or settable. The guard fails when the current list differs in either
direction; a name that loses its status needs an entry in removals, with a reason, in the same change.

icon.reason: Icon image: an --icon-* name or a url() value. Token sets style colours and sizes, not image files.

runtime.reason: Written from JavaScript at render time (setProperty, an inline style binding or a Vue v-bind() in a style block), so a stylesheet value is overwritten.

unread.reason: Declared by Nextcloud but read nowhere in the release, so a value changes nothing.

foreign.--color-error-light: summer-breeze sets it for Conduction apps that read it with a fallback (docudesk, the decidiq family). Nextcloud 34 neither declares nor reads it.

--body-container-radius.reason: intentionally not overridden: it is a CONTAINER radius, like `--border-radius-container` and `-container-large` above, and this used to map it to the brand's CONTROL radius. On a brand whose controls are near-square (Zwolle: 2px) that squared off the whole app shell, because `#content` draws its `border-radius` from this variable. Left to Nextcloud, the shell keeps stock geometry: the base value is 0 and only the two TOP corners are rounded, from `--border-radius-large`: which IS themed above, so the brand still decides how round the shell reads.
